info.title: riot-proxy
info.description:
A self-hosted proxy between [Riot's public API](https://developer.riotgames.com/) and everything downstream of it. It holds one Riot key, spends it carefully, and gives its consumers their own keys and quotas.

- **Rate limits:** read from Riot's own response headers. Requests a user is waiting on go ahead of background work.
- **Caching and archive:** repeated reads are served from cache; matches are immutable and archived.
- **One error envelope:** `{"error":{"code","message","requestId","retryAfter?"}}`.

### Response headers

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-Cache` | `HIT`, `MISS`, `STALE`, `HIT-NEG` (a cached 404), `ARCHIVE` (from the match archive), `BYPASS` (`?refresh=true`) |
| `X-Cache-Age` | Age of the **content** in seconds, not of the last fetch |
| `X-Cache-Fetched-Age` | Seconds since the proxy last read it from Riot, changed or not. Not sent for `ARCHIVE` |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset` | Your consumer quota |
| `X-Request-Id` | Quote this when reporting a problem |
| `Retry-After` | On `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (429) and `RATE_LIMITED` (503): seconds to wait |

Each response in this document declares the headers it sends.

### Images

`/v1/static/*` serves Data Dragon's JSON. Its images are mirrored too, at `/ddragon/<version>/img/<kind>/<file>`: Data Dragon's own `/cdn/<version>/img/<kind>/<file>` layout, for `champion`, `profileicon`, `item` and `spell` (summoner spells). Rune icons are at `/ddragon/<version>/img/<icon>`, `icon` being `runesReforged.json`'s `perk-images/…` path. Both are declared under **Static data**. `<version>` may be any version in Riot's list (`/v1/static/versions`), so a match can use its own patch's icons (`ddragonVersion`); for a patch the mirror hasn't synced, the data file that lists the image is fetched first. The file must be one that version's data lists. An image is fetched from Riot's CDN on first request, then served from disk; the bytes never change, and are sent `immutable` for a year. `/ddragon` needs no key, and its errors have an empty body. CommunityDragon assets are not mirrored.

get.summary: A rune or rune style icon
get.description:
No key. The image is Data Dragon's own, fetched from Riot's CDN on its first request and served from disk after that.

**Versions.** Any version in Riot's version list (`/v1/static/versions`) works, not only the current one, so a match can draw its own patch's icons (`ddragonVersion` on the match page). For a version the mirror hasn't synced, the one data file that lists the image (that patch's `item.json` for an item) is fetched first and kept. A version Riot doesn't list is a 404 with no fetch.

**Immutable.** The bytes at a given version and path never change once served, so they are sent with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. A response that isn't a 200 has no `Cache-Control`.

**What can be fetched.** Only a file the version's own data lists, so a request can't make the proxy fetch anything else. Concurrent first requests for one file share one fetch, and a data file Riot has no copy of isn't asked for twice.

**Errors** have an empty body, not the JSON error envelope.

get.description: Answers as long as the process is up. It touches nothing, so a 200 says only that the process is serving; use `/readyz` to decide whether to send traffic.
Prometheus text exposition format, not JSON. Behind a reverse proxy, restrict this path to private ranges.

SQLite can take a write and the limiter checkpoint is restored. While the writer runs a write, `sqlite` says whether SQLite has made progress on it in the last 5 s instead of queueing a probe behind it, so a long rebuild stays ready and a stuck write does not. **The 503 carries the same body as the 200**, so the booleans name what is not ready. `sqliteReadersFree`, `writerBusy`, `writerBusyMs` and `writerQueued` are informational; they don't affect `ok`.

get.summary: Champion pick, ban and win rates
get.description: Aggregated from every archived match on the platform. Each participant is placed at the tier the ladder crawl or the latest league lookup of that player found them at, whichever is newer, and under `UNKNOWN` when neither has. Without `tier`, one row per champion summed over every tier (`tier: null`): pick and ban rates over every match in the slice (platform, queue, patch), each match counted once however many tiers its players were in, and averages over all the champion's games. With `tier`, a row per champion at that tier, its rates over the matches that had a player at the tier. `minGames` and `limit` apply to the rows returned. Recomputed per (platform, queue) when a crawl completes. Sends an `ETag`; a matching `If-None-Match` gets 304. Kept in memory until the next recompute: `X-Cache: HIT` from memory, `MISS` read from the tables. Games Riot flagged as remakes are left out unless `remakes=include`.

get.description:
Upgrade with `Authorization: Bearer rpx_…`, or `?token=rpx_…` from a browser. The server sends `{"op":"ready","consumer":…}`, then:

- `{"op":"subscribe","topics":[…]}` / `{"op":"unsubscribe","topics":[…]}` → `{"op":"subscribed","topics":[…]}`, listing everything the socket holds. A topic that was refused is absent.
- `{"op":"ping"}` → `{"op":"pong","at":…}`.
- Events arrive as `{"op":"event","event":…,"topic":…,"at":…,"data":{…}}`.
- `{"op":"resync","topic":…,"dropped":n}` means this socket fell behind and missed `n` events on that topic; re-read what it covers.
- Problems arrive as `{"op":"error","error":{"code","message"}}` without closing the socket.

**Topics:** `player:<puuid>` (game, rank and archive events for one player), `patch`, and admin only: `metrics` (a snapshot every `METRICS_INTERVAL_S` while subscribed), `ladder`, `firehose` (every event). At most 200 per socket. The server pings every 30 s and drops a socket after two unanswered pings.

**Events:** `game.started`, `game.ended`, `rank.changed`, `match.archived` (player topics); `patch.new`; `crawl.phase`, `ladder.crawl.completed`, `analytics.updated` (`ladder`); `metrics.snapshot` (`metrics`).

**Closes:** 4401 for an invalid or revoked key, 1001 on server shutdown.

rows.description: Rows the last runs wrote, all ladders.

Data Dragon's own directory names, `spell` being summoner spells. The
handler matches the path segment against `IMAGE_KINDS`; a test keeps the
two lists the same.

workers.description:
This process's workers, in order, each with its job's latest step. Empty in a process that

finished.description: Jobs that finished in this process since it started, newest first.

delayed.description: Pending but waiting out a backoff.

heldKinds.description:
Kinds with as many jobs running as `JOB_KIND_LIMITS` allows. Their rows in `next` wait for one to
finish; workers claim other kinds meanwhile.

held.description: Ready jobs of `heldKinds`, counted in `ready` too.

JobSummary.description: A row of the durable queue (design/06).

runAfter.description: Not before this instant; the backoff after a failure.

matched.description: Rows the filter matched when the purge started.

tierFloor.description: How far down the ladder this run was told to enumerate.

phase.description:
Which stage a running crawl is in. `enumerate` walks the ladder, `collect` gathers every
discovered player's match ids, and `archive` fetches the matches behind them — in that
order, so a match shared by ten players is fetched once.

backfillsEnqueued.description: Players whose match history the collect stage was asked to walk.

matchIdsSeen.description: Distinct matches those players have played, after de-duplication.

matchesQueued.description: How many of those were not already archived, and so cost a fetch.

pendingLegs.description:
Legs of the current stage still outstanding — apex leagues and (tier, division) walks,
then match-id batches, then the archive hand-off. 0 for a finished run.

apexCapped.description:
Apex tiers whose league Riot returned at its cap of 10,000 entries, e.g. `["MASTER"]`:
Riot lists only the top of those tiers, so the crawl is missing their lowest players.
`[]` when none.

entries.description: Ladder entries this key scope holds.

oneOf.description: What it did; null when it failed.

error.description: Why it failed; the job is retried like any other.

rank.description: The player's division within a tier.

interactiveWaiters.description: Interactive requests queued on this scope; bulk yields while any wait (ADM-04).

usage.description: Per-window usage as the limiter sees it; empty before Riot has named the limits.

frozenMs.description:
Milliseconds until a 429-induced freeze on this bucket lifts; 0 when it
is not frozen (v1 `isFrozen` answered 0, never null).

matchIds.description:
The id page as Riot returned it, including ids no summary could be built
for. With `champion`, the archive's ids for that champion instead.

matches.description: One summary per id that resolved: the requesting player's line in each game.

hasMore.description:
A full page came back, so there is probably another behind it. With
`champion` it is exact: the archive holds another game behind this page.

champion.description: Echoes the `champion` filter; absent without one.

oneOf.description: With `champion` only: how much of the player's history the page draws on.

matchIdsAgeSeconds.description:

same ids does not reset it.

matchIdsFetchedAgeSeconds.description: How long ago the id list was last read from Riot, whether or not it changed.

mirror has no version list yet or the list lacks the patch.

rewardConfig.description: Reward configuration. Not in every recorded body.

jobs.description:

carries a K/D/A.

about what this deployment has archived, not the player's whole history.

at.description: Unix ms when the response was ready.

v.description: Bumped only when a field changes meaning.

events.description: Frames published per event name since the process started.

inflight.description: Riot calls in flight, each shared by every request waiting on it (ADM-04).

quotas.description: Every consumer metered since the start, busiest first (ADM-04).

profileIconId.description: ID of the summoner icon associated with the summoner.

revisionDate.description: Date summoner was last modified specified as epoch milliseconds.

puuid.description: Encrypted PUUID. Exact length of 78 characters.

summonerLevel.description: Summoner level associated with the summoner.

attempt.description: Which attempt this trace is of.

nextSeq.description: The `seq` the next event will get; pass it back as `after`.

dropped.description: Events dropped from the front (only the last [`EVENTS_PER_JOB`] are kept).

nowSince.description: When the job got to that step.

events.description: Events the job has logged so far.

X-Cache-Fetched-Age.description: Seconds since the proxy last read it from Riot, changed or not. Not sent for `ARCHIVE`.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current minute.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until a request slot frees up.

X-Request-Id.description: This request's id; quote it when reporting a problem.

bearerAuth.description: A consumer key, `rpx_…`, issued by `riot-proxy key create` or `POST /v1/admin/consumers` and shown exactly once. Only its SHA-256 is stored.
